scenes.tts: The first film tested inheritance models against family observations. How can learning that someone is unaffected raise their carrier probability? The surprise comes from comparing only genotypes still compatible with the observation.
scenes.caption: The first film tested inheritance models against family observations. How can learning that someone is unaffected raise their carrier probability? The surprise comes from comparing only genotypes still compatible with the observation.
scenes.visual: REUSE THE FIRST FILM'S COLOUR MAP: inheritance routes GOLD; affected phenotypes RED; compatible possibilities TEAL; excluded or downweighted possibilities VIOLET; unaffected symbols WHITE. A small pedigree enters from left. On the right, equal genotype tiles fill a probability bar. An unaffected observation card hovers above them like a filter.
scenes.narration: The first film tested inheritance models against family observations. How can learning that someone is unaffected raise their carrier probability? The surprise comes from comparing only genotypes still compatible with the observation.

scenes.visual: The observation card slides halfway through the bar without changing it. Title 'Evidence Reweights the Possibilities' appears briefly, then shrinks into a label above the bar.

scenes.tts: Begin with every genotype the inheritance model allows. Give each possibility its starting weight before using the person's phenotype. These weights come from transmission rules and any population assumptions. Write them down before looking at the answer you hope to get.
scenes.caption: Begin with every genotype the inheritance model allows. Give each possibility its starting weight before using the person's phenotype. These weights come from transmission rules and any population assumptions. Write them down before looking at the answer you hope to get.
scenes.visual: The probability bar separates into genotype tiles labelled with letters on screen. Equal widths show equal starting weights. GOLD allele bars move from the parents in the pedigree into each tile, showing how the model generated them.
scenes.narration: Begin with every genotype the inheritance model allows. Give each possibility its starting weight before using the person's phenotype. These weights come from transmission rules and any population assumptions. Write them down before looking at the answer you hope to get.

scenes.tts: Now condition on what you observed. Any genotype incompatible with that observation loses its weight. Compatible possibilities remain. This is a filter, not a change to the person's cells. Keep the survivors in their original proportions.
scenes.caption: Now condition on what you observed. Any genotype incompatible with that observation loses its weight. Compatible possibilities remain. This is a filter, not a change to the person's cells. Keep the survivors in their original proportions.
scenes.visual: The WHITE unaffected observation card passes over the tiles. One phenotype-incompatible tile turns VIOLET and shrinks to zero. The compatible tiles glow TEAL but keep their relative widths for the moment.
scenes.narration: Now condition on what you observed. Any genotype incompatible with that observation loses its weight. Compatible possibilities remain. This is a filter, not a change to the person's cells. Keep the survivors in their original proportions.

scenes.tts: Suppose a new observation excludes one visible possibility. Which tiles should remain in the probability bar, and what must happen next? Watch the total bar, not just the disappearing tile.
scenes.caption: Suppose a new observation excludes one visible possibility. Which tiles should remain in the probability bar, and what must happen next? Watch the total bar, not just the disappearing tile.
scenes.visual: Reset to a generic bar with several labelled tiles. A VIOLET observation card points to one incompatible tile. Show the question 'Remove it—then what?' while all tiles drift gently.
scenes.narration: Suppose a new observation excludes one visible possibility. Which tiles should remain in the probability bar, and what must happen next? Watch the total bar, not just the disappearing tile.

scenes.visual: Deliberate prediction pause. The incompatible tile pulses VIOLET; compatible tiles breathe TEAL. The total-width bracket above the bar remains fixed.

scenes.tts: Remove the incompatible tile. Then stretch the survivors to fill the whole bar again. That second step is renormalizing. The surviving possibilities now divide all the probability between them.
scenes.caption: Remove the incompatible tile. Then stretch the survivors to fill the whole bar again. That second step is renormalizing. The surviving possibilities now divide all the probability between them.
scenes.visual: The VIOLET tile folds away. The TEAL survivors expand smoothly until they fill the fixed total-width bracket. Add the label 'renormalize: total probability stays whole' beneath the moving bar.
scenes.narration: Remove the incompatible tile. Then stretch the survivors to fill the whole bar again. That second step is renormalizing. The surviving possibilities now divide all the probability between them.

scenes.tts: A carrier tile can therefore occupy more of the remaining bar. This can happen even when the person is unaffected. The comparison set became smaller.
scenes.caption: A carrier tile can therefore occupy more of the remaining bar. This can happen even when the person is unaffected. The comparison set became smaller.
scenes.visual: Highlight a TEAL carrier tile as it widens after the affected tile disappears. The WHITE person symbol stays unchanged. A vertical divider shows 'before evidence' beside 'after evidence'; label both displays 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A carrier tile can therefore occupy more of the remaining bar. This can happen even when the person is unaffected. The comparison set became smaller.

scenes.tts: Nothing happened to the person's D N A. Evidence changes genotype probabilities, not genotypes. Only the description of your uncertainty changed.
scenes.caption: Nothing happened to the person's DNA. Evidence changes genotype probabilities, not genotypes. Only the description of your uncertainty changed.
scenes.visual: The person's chromosome bars remain fixed while the probability bar changes shape behind them. Put a small lock on the chromosome bars and a moving magnifying glass over the bar.
scenes.narration: Nothing happened to the person's DNA. Evidence changes genotype probabilities, not genotypes. Only the description of your uncertainty changed.

scenes.tts: Sometimes evidence does not eliminate a hypothesis. It is merely more likely under one hypothesis than another. Bayes' rule handles that case. The observation changes weights without making either hypothesis impossible. Likelihood measures that predictive fit.
scenes.caption: Sometimes evidence does not eliminate a hypothesis. It is merely more likely under one hypothesis than another. Bayes' rule handles that case. The observation changes weights without making either hypothesis impossible. Likelihood measures that predictive fit.
scenes.visual: Transform the genotype bar into two hypothesis columns, both starting at equal height. An evidence card sends a thick TEAL stream into one column and a thin stream into the other. Label the stream widths 'likelihood — schematic'.
scenes.narration: Sometimes evidence does not eliminate a hypothesis. It is merely more likely under one hypothesis than another. Bayes' rule handles that case. The observation changes weights without making either hypothesis impossible. Likelihood measures that predictive fit.

scenes.tts: Each hypothesis starts with a prior weight. Multiply that weight by how well the hypothesis predicts the observation. A better prediction earns a larger updated weight. A weak prediction earns less.
scenes.caption: Each hypothesis starts with a prior weight. Multiply that weight by how well the hypothesis predicts the observation. A better prediction earns a larger updated weight. A weak prediction earns less.
scenes.visual: Each column becomes two joined blocks: GOLD 'prior' below and TEAL 'likelihood' above. The blocks compress into a single weighted tile per hypothesis. No arithmetic is narrated; symbolic multiplication appears on screen.
scenes.narration: Each hypothesis starts with a prior weight. Multiply that weight by how well the hypothesis predicts the observation. A better prediction earns a larger updated weight. A weak prediction earns less.

scenes.tts: Finally, renormalize those weighted hypotheses. Their new shares form the posterior: the probabilities after accounting for the evidence. Together, those shares still fill the complete probability bar.
scenes.caption: Finally, renormalize those weighted hypotheses. Their new shares form the posterior: the probabilities after accounting for the evidence. Together, those shares still fill the complete probability bar.
scenes.visual: The weighted hypothesis tiles slide into one fixed-width bar and expand proportionally. Label the completed bar 'posterior'. A thin arrow connects prior bar, evidence filter, and posterior bar without changing the pedigree.
scenes.narration: Finally, renormalize those weighted hypotheses. Their new shares form the posterior: the probabilities after accounting for the evidence. Together, those shares still fill the complete probability bar.

scenes.tts: More observations repeat the same cycle. Start with current weights, ask what each hypothesis predicts, apply the evidence, then renormalize. Each new fact becomes the next filter. The method remains the same.
scenes.caption: More observations repeat the same cycle. Start with current weights, ask what each hypothesis predicts, apply the evidence, then renormalize. Each new fact becomes the next filter. The method remains the same.
scenes.visual: Build a circular four-step track around the pedigree: 'current weights', 'prediction', 'evidence', 'renormalize'. A GOLD marker travels around once while the probability bar changes at each step.
scenes.narration: More observations repeat the same cycle. Start with current weights, ask what each hypothesis predicts, apply the evidence, then renormalize. Each new fact becomes the next filter. The method remains the same.

scenes.tts: The answer still depends on the model. Penetrance, new mutation, family relationships, and population assumptions all shape those starting weights and likelihoods. If an assumption changes, recompute instead of reusing the old answer.
scenes.caption: The answer still depends on the model. Penetrance, new mutation, family relationships, and population assumptions all shape those starting weights and likelihoods. If an assumption changes, recompute instead of reusing the old answer.
scenes.visual: Four assumption cards slide under the probability bar as its foundation. Removing any card makes the bar wobble, not collapse. Keep every value schematic and show no clinical certainty label.
scenes.narration: The answer still depends on the model. Penetrance, new mutation, family relationships, and population assumptions all shape those starting weights and likelihoods. If an assumption changes, recompute instead of reusing the old answer.

scenes.tts: With that picture, the text can calculate exact carrier and recurrence probabilities. Keep the filter, the weights, and the assumptions visible. The worked examples begin with different family evidence.
scenes.caption: With that picture, the text can calculate exact carrier and recurrence probabilities. Keep the filter, the weights, and the assumptions visible. The worked examples begin with different family evidence.
scenes.visual: The generic bar and pedigree shrink into the corner of a clean worksheet frame. Empty equation slots appear without answers. The three labels 'filter', 'weights', and 'assumptions' remain large and bright.
scenes.narration: With that picture, the text can calculate exact carrier and recurrence probabilities. Keep the filter, the weights, and the assumptions visible. The worked examples begin with different family evidence.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only: 'Evidence changes genotype probabilities, not genotypes.' Behind it, the probability bar gently resizes while locked chromosome bars remain fixed.
